doc.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Playing on Ricky Martin's She Bangs
summary: A studio story about the title and the hit record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I remember in the studio, I’m in the studio and I’ve got this music in front of me it says “She Bangs,” and like I’m the oldest guy in the horn section of the thing and I says, “Jesus, when I was a kid,” I said, “I never heard that expression.” I says, “The expression I heard when I was a kid was she gang bangs.” And I couldn’t believe that this thing was actually going to come out under that title. And all of a sudden the record came out and it’s called “She Bangs.” Right? That was the tune. And so I’m up at the beach in Rhode Island and these little kids around me and their father and everything else, and I said I did this Ricky Martin, “You worked with Ricky Martin?” he said. So I had to tell the father like yeah it was — and then the thing becomes the biggest hit in the country. I mean it’s like a monster hit you know. “She Bangs.”
